How SQLite Stores Rows

SQLite keeps every table in a B-tree. Each row has a 64-bit row ID, and the rows are stored in the leaf pages of that tree, sorted by row ID.

When a page fills up, SQLite splits it into two pages and updates the parent. This is why inserts stay fast even when the table grows to millions of rows.
